prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1131; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a sideswipe that occurred while the insured's vehicle was changing lanes. The claimant reports a knee injury and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the coverage was in force at the time of the incident. Nothing so far suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact. Requested photos from the scene and the repair facility.

Entry 4: Photos received. They confirm several points of the described impact, including contact along the passenger side panel. No independent witnesses have come forward to date.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant by phone. The account of the lane change and the contact matches the initial report, and the claimant described the knee injury without any changes to the earlier statement.

Entry 6: Reviewed the damage estimate. The damage is mostly consistent with the described impact. A few old scratches near the rear quarter panel may predate this crash, so the appraiser has been asked to note them separately.

Entry 7: Obtained the medical summary. The reported knee injury is plausible for a collision of this type. No prior injury to the same body area is on record.

Entry 8: Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of knee injury. Requested the treating provider's notes to understand the timeline of care.

Entry 9: Follow-up call with the claimant. The claimant repeated the same account of events as in every prior conversation, with no new details added or removed.

Entry 10: Reviewed the provider notes and the photos together. The overall picture is consistent with the reported crash. The extended treatment period remains the main open question and is being monitored.

Entry 11: File updated with current findings. Injury evaluation and the separate note on the older scratches remain pending before the claim is finalized.
